recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Renaming enableBehavior or requiring it for a single enableWhen would conflict with the applied current model and later published corrections; no follow-up core source work is recommended for FHIR-15664.
issue_request: FHIR-15664 was a Published FHIR-core Questionnaire change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3, asking that multiple Questionnaire.item.enableWhen conditions not always be joined as OR. The resolution requested an all/any code element, an invariant requiring that behavior control when multiple enableWhen criteria need disambiguation, and removal of old unconditional OR wording.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in commit 651aa532afe40d621b6a593df3fabc0b86b0af62, a historical Questionnaire spreadsheet commit for GF#15664. That commit added Questionnaire.item.enableBehavior with binding name EnableWhenBehavior and all/any semantics, though the old always-OR wording still remained in the initial enableWhen comment until later clarification work.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. Later Published Questionnaire issues refined the same area: FHIR-26993 rewrote the enableWhen comment to point to enableBehavior and distinguish multiple enableWhen repetitions from multiple answers; FHIR-26831 and FHIR-32526 corrected que-12 so enableBehavior is required when enableWhen.count() > 1. These later decisions confirm that the current element name and invariant threshold are intentional.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml defines Questionnaire.item.enableBehavior as a 0..1 code with a required binding to ValueSet/questionnaire-enable-behavior, documents all/any behavior, points the enableWhen comment to enableBehavior rather than unconditional OR semantics, and carries que-12 as enableWhen.count() > 1 implies enableBehavior.exists(). The companion CodeSystem defines the all and any codes.
